simple.meaning: שָׁלַשׁ (shâlash) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to be (causatively, make ) triplicate (by restoration, in portions, strands, days or years).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 9 times across Genesis, Deuteronomy, 1 Samuel, 1 Kings, Ecclesiastes, and 1 more, beginning at Genesis 15:9. Its contexts include land.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שָׁלַשׁ (H8027).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: שָׁלַשׁ (shâlash) / H8027 is traced through Genesis 15:9, Deuteronomy 19:3, 1 Samuel 20:19, 1 Kings 18:34 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.short: to be (causatively, make ) triplicate (by restoration, in portions, strands, days or years)
definitions.usage: do the third time, (divide into, stay) three (days, -fold, parts, years old).
definitions.full: H8027. shalash I. Pu`al Participle מְשֻׁלָּשׁ three years old Gen 15:9 + 1Sam 1:24 (read with ᵐ5 Th We etc. מְשֻׁלָּשׁ בְּפַר for שְׁלשָׁה בְּפָרִם ), feminine מְשֻׁלֶּשֶׁת Gen 15:9 (twice in verse); הַמְשֻׁלָּשׁ הַחוּט Eccl 4:12 the threefold cord ; female plural מְשֻׁלָּשׁוֺת Ezek 42:6 three-storied chambers.
definitions.rootNote: a primitive root perhaps originally to intensify, i.e. treble; but apparently used only as denominative from 7969 ,
